title: Regulatory and Compliance, Corporate AML Oversight - Vice President
description: About the Role iCapital is seeking a Corporate Anti-Money Laundering (AML) Oversight Vice President to join its Regulatory and Compliance organization and support the AML team. This individual will serve as a senior subject-matter expert responsible for providing oversight of AML controls across applicable U.S. and international businesses. This role will partner closely with Legal, Compliance, Risk, business stakeholders, and other control functions to assess regulatory requirements, oversee the effectiveness of the AML control environment, identify emerging risks, and support the firm's ongoing regulatory readiness. Responsibilities Support the oversight, maintenance, and ongoing enhancement of the firm’s U.S. AML/CFT compliance framework, including policies, procedures, standards, internal controls, governance, and monitoring. Monitor developments involving applicable BSA, FinCEN, OFAC, SEC, and FINRA requirements and translate regulatory changes and emerging expectations into practical enhancements to the firm’s AML control environment. Provide AML subject-matter expertise and guidance to Compliance, Legal, Risk, Operations, Product, Technology, and business stakeholders. Evaluate new products, services, distribution arrangements, client relationships, and business initiatives for potential AML/CFT and sanctions implications and recommend appropriate risk mitigation. Facilitate enterprise and business-specific AML/CFT risk assessments, identify control gaps and enhancement opportunities, and establish oversight metrics and management information to monitor trends and areas requiring escalation. Provide Compliance oversight of higher-risk customer, investor, intermediary, and counterparty relationships, including AML/KYC escalations involving sanctions exposure, politically exposed persons, adverse media, complex ownership structures, jurisdictional risk, and other elevated financial-crime concerns. Advise stakeholders on enhanced due diligence, risk mitigation, escalation, and disposition, and support investigations involving potentially unusual or suspicious activity through the firm’s established SAR governance process. Assist with senior-management and committee reporting on AML risk, regulatory developments, significant issues, remediation initiatives, and program effectiveness while maintaining clear documentation of the firm’s AML governance and oversight framework. Coordinate and support AML-related regulatory examinations, internal audits, independent testing, compliance reviews, and regulatory information requests, ensuring responses and supporting documentation are complete and appropriately supported. Provide oversight of third parties performing AML/KYC activities, including developing risk-based due diligence, monitoring, and testing standards and assessing policies, controls, staffing, systems, screening practices, escalation processes, and regulatory adherence. Escalate material third-party or program deficiencies and oversee corrective-action and remediation plans in coordination with relevant Compliance, Operations, Legal, Technology, and business stakeholders. Support the development and delivery of risk-based AML/CFT training and targeted guidance on regulatory expectations, emerging financial-crime risks, escalation requirements, and AML red flags to promote consistent application of AML standards across U.S. businesses. Qualifications 10+ years of relevant experience in AML and BSA, financial crimes, regulatory compliance, or related risk-management roles within financial services Bachelor's degree is required; JD, advanced degree, or other relevant professional certification is a plus Significant experience within a broker-dealer, investment adviser, asset manager, private funds organization, bank, or comparable regulated financial institution Strong working knowledge of the Bank Secrecy Act, USA PATRIOT Act, FinCEN regulations and guidance, OFAC requirements, FINRA AML requirements, and relevant SEC requirements and expectations Experience assessing complex legal entities, private investment structures, funds, financial intermediaries, or institutional relationships strongly preferred Able to interpret regulatory requirements and translate them into practical controls and governance standards Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate complex regulatory matters to senior management and business stakeholders Demonstrated ability to challenge existing processes constructively and drive remediation across multiple functions CAMS certification is strongly preferred Benefits The base salary range for this role is $155,000 to $180,000.  iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, tele

title: Senior Manager, Valuation
description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role Robinhood is seeking a Senior Manager, Valuation to lead and execute valuation analyses for private company investments, minority equity stakes, and other illiquid financial instruments held across the organization. This role will partner closely with Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting (TAFR), Corporate Development, and the RHV Private Markets Valuation Committee to ensure valuations are well-supported, defensible, and compliant with US GAAP (ASC 820, ASC 321/323) and SEC reporting requirements. This role reports into Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting (TAFR) leadership and works closely with the RHV Private Markets Valuation Committee. This role is based in our Menlo Park, CA, New York, NY, and Chicago, IL office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams.  What you’ll do Financial Modeling & Valuation Analysis Build and maintain complex financial models (DCF, comparable company/precedent transaction analyses, OPM/PWERM, Monte Carlo simulations) to support fair value measurements of private company investments and other illiquid holdings. Perform quarterly and event-driven valuations for private equity/venture-style investments, including waterfall/allocation analyses across complex capital structures (preferred stock, SAFEs, convertible notes, warrants). Develop and refine valuation methodologies in line with AICPA Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation Guidelines. Governance & Reporting Prepare valuation memos and supporting documentation for presentation to the RHV Private Markets Valuation Committee and Audit Committee. Partner with TAFR to ensure valuation conclusions are properly reflected in consolidated financial statements and SEC disclosures (10-Q/10-K, 8-K as applicable). Serve as a key point of contact for external auditors (EY) on valuation-related audit requests, walkthroughs, and testing. Cross-Functional Partnership Collaborate with Corporate Development, Legal, and Investor Relations on new investment structuring, follow-on financings, and exit/liquidity events to assess valuation impacts. Advise on the accounting and valuation implications of new or complex investment structures (e.g., tiered/contingent consideration, equity-linked instruments). Process & Controls Maintain and enhance internal controls (SOX) over the valuation process, including documentation standards, model governance, and data source validation. Drive continuous improvement of valuation templates, market data inputs, and benchmarking practices. What you bring Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or related field. 10+ years of relevant experience in valuation, financial modeling, investment banking, or private equity/venture capital, with a focus on private company or illiquid investment valuation. Demonstrated expertise in building and auditing complex financial models (DCF, comparable company analysis, option pricing models, waterfall/allocation models). Strong working knowledge of US GAAP fair value measurement guidance (ASC 820) and its application to private investments. Excellent communication skills, with experience presenting valuation conclusions to committees, auditors, or senior stakeholders. Advanced proficiency in Excel/financial modeling; familiarity with valuation software or platforms a plus. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not.  Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus

title: Finance Transformation Governance, Managing Director
description: Who we are looking for The Managing Director, Finance Transformation Governance will lead the governance, risk, and control strategy supporting Finance's transformation agenda. This executive will be responsible for ensuring that business process redesign, automation, technology implementations, data initiatives, and operating model changes are executed within a robust governance and control framework. As a strategic leader within Finance, the Managing Director will establish and oversee a comprehensive framework to assess the impact of transformation initiatives on Finance processes, risks, controls, regulatory obligations, and policy compliance. The role will serve as a key partner to Finance Transformation, Controllership, Regulatory Reporting, Finance Business Risk Management (BRM), Technology, Compliance, and Enterprise Risk teams to ensure that transformation efforts strengthen operational effectiveness while maintaining a sound control environment. The successful candidate will drive the integration of risk and control considerations into transformation design, promote the adoption of automated and preventive controls, and ensure that Finance remains aligned with enterprise policies, governance standards, and regulatory expectations throughout periods of change. What you will be responsible for Establish and Lead the Finance Transformation Governance Framework Design and implement the governance framework supporting Finance transformation initiatives across the organization. Establish standards, methodologies, and decision-making processes to evaluate transformation activities from a governance, risk, and control perspective. Develop executive reporting, metrics, and governance forums to provide transparency into transformation program risks, dependencies, control impacts, and remediation activities. Advise senior Finance leadership on governance implications associated with strategic investments, organizational redesign, automation initiatives, and technology implementations. Serve as the primary Finance governance leader overseeing the intersection of transformation execution, risk management, and internal controls. Assess Transformation Impacts on Finance Processes and Controls Establish a consistent framework to identify and assess the impact of transformation initiatives on end-to-end Finance processes, key controls, regulatory reporting obligations, and financial risk management activities. Ensure that process, control, data, and technology impacts are evaluated before significant transformation initiatives are approved and implemented. Lead reviews of future-state operating models to identify emerging risks, control gaps, segregation of duty concerns, and compliance considerations. Oversee process inventories and process mapping efforts to maintain an accurate understanding of how transformation activities affect the Finance control environment. Provide effective challenge and independent review of transformation programs to ensure risks are identified and appropriately mitigated. Drive Control Design for Automated and Digital Processes Lead the development of Finance's strategy for embedding automated, preventive, and technology-enabled controls within transformed business processes. Partner with Finance Transformation, Technology, and BRM teams to design controls that support new digital workflows, automation tools, AI-enabled solutions, and system implementations. Develop standards and guidance for control rationalization, control automation, and control modernization initiatives. Ensure newly designed controls are sustainable, auditable, scalable, and compliant with regulatory and enterprise requirements. Promote reduction of manual controls through implementation of automated monitoring and preventive control solutions. Partner Across Finance Business Risk Management Establish strong partnerships across Finance Business Risk Management functions to ensure consistent risk and control practices during transformation initiatives. Coordinate with SOX, Regulatory Reporting, Operational Risk, Issue Management, and Control Testing teams to identify and address transformation-related risks. Ensure transformation programs maintain appropriate risk assessments, control documentation, issue management, and testing requirements. Drive consistency in governance and control standards across Finance organizations undergoing change. Serve as a senior escalation point for transformation-related risk and control matters. Ensure Alignment with Enterprise Governance and Policy Requirements Partner closely with Enterprise Risk Management, Compliance, Legal, Technology Risk, Operational Risk, Corporate Audit, and Corporate Governance functions across the organization. Ensure Finance transformation programs comply with enterprise policies, standards, risk frameworks, and governance requirements. title: Technical Accounting & Reporting Senior Manager
description: From Fivetran’s founding until now, our mission has remained the same: to make access to data as simple and reliable as electricity. With Fivetran, customer data arrives in their warehouses, canonical and ready to query, with no engineering or maintenance required. We’re proud that more organizations continue to leverage our technology every day to become truly data-driven. About Us Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data. Together, we’re delivering the data infrastructure layer that helps organizations move, transform, and trust their data — from the moment data moves, through every transformation, to the context teams and AI systems rely on. Fivetran helps organizations automate data movement across the systems, clouds, engines, and tools they rely on. dbt Labs pioneered analytics engineering, helping teams transform data into reliable, governed insights. Together, we support thousands of organizations as they build a trusted foundation for analytics, AI, and better business decisions. As we bring our teams and technology together, we’re building on the strengths of both companies while continuing to deliver the products and experiences our customers know and trust. It’s an exciting time to join us: we’re creating a company with the scale, talent, and technology to help more organizations put their data to work with greater speed, confidence, and impact. During this transition period, you may see references to both Fivetran and dbt Labs throughout our recruiting process as we integrate our teams, systems, and career sites. About the Role Fivetran is building data pipelines to power the modern data stack for thousands of companies. We’re looking for a self-motivated, detail-oriented, and technically proficient Technical Accounting & Financial Reporting Senior Manager . This individual will play a key role in supporting complex accounting matters, building scalable processes, collaborating cross-functionally, and contributing to a strong internal control and reporting environment that meets the standards of a sophisticated, fast-growing SaaS company. This is a full-time position based out of our Denver office. Our hybrid work model offers a blend of remote flexibility and in-person collaboration, including two days in the office each week to connect and build as a team. What You’ll Do Research, analyze, and document technical accounting issues and memos and prepare calculations to support accounting conclusions and facilitate external audit reviews in accordance with US GAAP, including but not limited to ASC 718 (Stock-Based Compensation), ASC 350-40 (Capitalized Software), ASC 340 (Capitalized Commissions), ASC 805 (Business Combinations), ASC 842 (Leases), and ASC 480 (Debt & Equity). Develop and maintain accounting policies and procedures, and lead implementation of significant changes. Work with external valuation specialists to ensure complex transaction valuations are completed accurately and on time, including managing inputs and reviewing deliverables for 409A valuations, intangible asset valuations, and equity award valuations. Collaborate with teams across Accounting Operations, Engineering, Finance, Legal, HR, and other departments to ensure technical guidance is consistently operationalized and understood. Support initiatives to enhance external reporting readiness, including complex accounting topics, disclosures, and process improvements. Help design and implement efficient, SOX-compliant accounting processes and internal controls to support organizational growth. Partner with external auditors and consultants to ensure timely and accurate conclusions on accounting matters. Provide training and mentorship to team members on technical accounting topics and emerging standards. Skills We’re Looking For Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance required; CPA license required 7+ years of combined experience in Big 4 public accounting and/or corporate accounting at a SaaS or high-growth technology company Demonstrated technical accounting expertise and experience drafting memos on complex, non-routine transactions Strong understanding of US GAAP and internal control frameworks (e.g., SOX) Experience working in or supporting a company with increasing external reporting, audit, or regulatory complexity Familiarity with ERP systems and financial reporting tools (Netsuite and Workiva preferred) and a mindset toward process improvement and automation Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to collaborate across departments Self-starter with strong organizational skills and attention to detail; comfortable working independently in a high-growth, fast-paced environment. Bonus Skills​ Prior experience as part of an S-1 filing or IPO project team. Experience with automation and AI tools to drive efficiency. #LI-JG1 #LI-Hybrid The compensation range displayed

title: Manager, GRC
description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At  Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.”  learn more about working at Coinbase . We're hiring a Manager, GRC to join our Technology Risk & Controls team within Security and lead second line of defense advisory coverage across critical technology and security domains. This team evaluates risk posture, improves control design, and helps engineering, infrastructure, and security leaders make better, risk-informed decisions. You'll both manage a team and directly own advisory coverage for domains that may include disaster recovery and resiliency, SDLC, artificial intelligence, identity and access management, and supply chain - building trusted partnerships that ensure Coinbase addresses its most critical risks in its most critical functions. What you'll do: Lead second line advisory coverage for key technology and security domains, assessing risk exposure, control effectiveness, policy alignment, and emerging issues across the business. Partner with engineering and technology teams to evaluate domain posture and identify where additional controls, remediation, or governance improvements are needed. Review and challenge the design of new and existing risks and their corresponding controls to ensure our mitigations are scalable, effective, and aligned to business, risk, and regulatory expectations.  Drive coordination across risk, controls, policy, audit, and assurance teams to translate incidents, audit findings, and regulatory expectations into actionable improvements that strengthen the technology control environment. Intake, triage, and calculate inherent and residual risk with subject matter experts and risk owners, facilitating risk treatment decisions and validating execution of mitigation plans. Enable leadership decision-making by communicating quantitative and qualitative risk tradeoffs and connecting risks, controls, policies, incidents, and findings into clear narratives that support prioritization and reporting. Build, grow, and coach a team of technology and security analysts and senior analysts, fostering a culture of agility, innovation, and continuous performance feedback. Required Skills and Experience: 8+ years in technology risk, IT controls, IT audit, cybersecurity risk, or compliance, with hands-on experience delivering full-stack GRC services (risk management, control design, continuous monitoring, governance documentation) - not a controls-only or risk-only background. Deep understanding of technical design and governance principles across one or more domains such as infrastructure resiliency, SDLC, change management, or incident response, with demonstrated ability to challenge status quo and drive improvement. Hands-on experience evaluating risks and control design, identifying weaknesses, and partnering with stakeholders to improve risk outcomes and control maturity. Proven track record managing and mentoring analysts, growing their capabilities and careers while holding teams accountable to deliverables and timelines. Track record of influencing cross-functional stakeholders, navigating ambiguity, and translating complex risk and compliance concepts into clear functional requirements for both technical and non-technical audiences. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.  Position ID:  P78170 #LI-Remote Pay Transparency Notice: Base salary varies by location (see range below). title: Finance Director - Retail Beauty
description: About THG   We are THG, a global ecommerce group on a mission to be the global online leader in beauty and sports nutrition.   Our portfolio of leading retailers and brands such as LOOKFANTASTIC, Myprotein, ESPA, Perricone MD, and Cult Beauty form our two core businesses: THG Beauty and THG Nutrition.   From Manchester to New York, we’re powered by a team of over 2500 people who work together, lead by example, and think BIG.    With us, you’ll go further, faster. What are you waiting for?   About Finance at THG THG Finance is a dynamic and evolving team that covers all areas of finance, including central functions such as accounts receivable and payable, treasury, tax, and internal audit, as well as specific commercial teams for each of our divisions; Beauty, Tech, Consumer, Health, and Brands. As we expand our business and take on new challenges in the form of acquired businesses or new ventures, finance is there to support every step of the way, leading to dynamic and challenging roles. Common characteristics among our team members are the ability to drive change, adaptability, and resourcefulness to ensure we can keep pace with the business, without compromising on financial control or sales performance. Responsibilities: Reporting into the Commercial CFO, the role is split into the below key areas: Financial Control & Reporting Full ownership of divisional month‑end close processes across all Nutrition brands, including Myprotein. Build and lead the Nutrition consolidation and group reporting process following business separation. Ensure rigorous balance sheet governance, accuracy, and control across all teams. Commercial Finance & Performance Management Lead commercial insights and analysis, challenging all aspects of the P&L to drive profitability. Deliver profit improvement and working capital initiatives across the division. Oversee budgeting and forecasting, providing both in‑month insight and rolling 12‑month projections to support strategic decision-making. Strategic Leadership & Business Partnering Support major strategic programmes including international expansion, organisational transformation, and business separation. Partner across all areas of the business—including supply chain, trading, and marketing—to ensure investments drive sustainable, profitable growth. Work collaboratively with group finance functions such as Tax, Treasury, and Group Reporting to ensure seamless alignment and compliance. Team Leadership & Operations Excellence Lead, motivate, and develop a multi‑disciplinary finance team of up to 25 colleagues. Oversee day‑to‑day finance operations, ensuring an efficient, well‑controlled, and high‑performing finance function. Drive a proactive, solutions‑led approach to identifying risks and opportunities across the short, medium, and long term. Within these areas the role will require: An inspirational leader, who thrives on being able to drive and work with an ambitious team to achieve goals aligned to the business’ need. A proactive approach to P&L performance, acting quickly on both risks and opportunities identified in both the short, medium and long term. A confident mindset, comfortable in dealing with a wide range of non-financial key stakeholders and managing difficult conversations. Comfortable to challenge and review spend approvals to ensure all costs deliver incremental benefit to the business. A strong attention to detail to ensure a tightly controlled balance sheet is delivered consistently, reviewing the wider team’s work. A keen ability to multi-task across a number of areas and manage both their own and the teams time effectively. An ability to communicate with wider finance functions outside of the division, including Group, Tax, Treasury etc, to ensure all relevant information is provided and received for reporting purposes. A collaborative approach to working with the wider divisional finance team including commercial, to assist with reporting and profit delivery, and SSC, to ensure a tightly controlled working capital cycle Requirements: Essential Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA, CIMA) with significant senior finance leadership experience in a complex, international organisation. Proven end‑to‑end ownership of P&L and Balance Sheet, with strong expertise in financial control, reporting, consolidation, and compliance. Demonstrated track record in commercial finance, including profit improvement, cost management, working capital optimisation, budgeting and forecasting. A credible and influential strategic partner, confident in challenging and guiding non‑financial stakeholders at all levels. Experience supporting major strategic initiatives such as international expansion, transformation programmes, or business separations. Strong people leader with experience managing and developing large, multi‑disciplinary finance teams. Exceptional attention to detail combined with the ability to operate strategically across a broad agenda. Excellent communicator capable of operating effectively across divisional and group finance environments. Desirable Experience in consumer goods, beauty, personal care, or FMCG sectors. Exposure to international business models. A good understanding of ecommerce. Track record of driving finance transformation, systems optimisation, and process improvements. What's in it for me? Career Development Access bespoke development programmes that have been designed and developed by our in-house L&D team. Continued development through our upskilling programme that is delivered in partnership with an industry-leading training provider. Enhanced Leave 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays. Don’t want to work on your birthday? We don’t either! Enjoy your day off on us! Enhanced maternity and paternity pay, depending on length of service. Up to 10 days compassionate leave. Buy back up to 3 days each year. Unlock 2 days volunteer leave after 12-months.   THG is proud to be a Disability Confident Committed employer. If you are invited to interview, please let us know if there are any reasonable adjustments we can make to the recruitment process that will enable you to perform to the best of your ability. THG is committed to creating a diverse & inclusive environment and hence welcomes applications from all sections of the community. Because of the high volumes of applications our opportunities attract, it sometimes takes us time to review and consider them all. We endeavour to respond to every application we receive within 14 days. If you haven't heard from us within that time frame or should you have any specific questions about this or other applications for positions at THG please contact one of our Talent team to discuss further. title: Head of Finance
description: PART-TIME 25 HOURS/WEEK, OPEN TO FULL-TIME. ABOUT THE ROLE Pika is seeking a strategic and experienced Head of Finance to join our on-site team in Palo Alto. As Head of Finance, you will be responsible for the overall financial leadership of the company, driving strategy, planning, compliance, and execution to enable our next phase of growth as a creative AI leader. You’ll work closely with the executive team to ensure financial health, transparency, and effective resource allocation, guiding Pika’s business decisions and growth strategy. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Lead and oversee all aspects of Pika’s financial operations, including accounting, FP&A, budgeting, treasury, AP/AR, and payroll - Build and manage scalable financial planning, modeling, and forecasting processes to guide executive decision-making - Develop and drive the company’s financial strategy, including long-term planning, fundraising support, and cross-functional resource allocation - Direct timely and accurate month-end and year-end close, financial reporting, statutory audits, and tax filings - Ensure compliance with all local, state, and federal regulations, as well as GAAP and internal controls - Monitor key financial indicators and provide proactive insights on risks, opportunities, and performance trends - Set up and manage financial systems and controls necessary for a high-growth, venture-backed environment - Partner with leadership across departments (Product, Sales, Operations) to evaluate and support business initiatives and company-wide strategy WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR - 7+ years of progressive finance leadership, including experience managing a finance team in a high-growth company or startup - Demonstrated expertise in financial modeling, forecasting, accounting principles, and business analytics - Broad experience managing full-stack finance functions, including budgeting, treasury, compliance, and internal controls - Strong track record of supporting fundraising, investor reporting, and board deliverables - Meticulous attention to detail and exceptional organization and leadership skills - Excellent communication and interpersonal abilities, with confidence presenting to C-suite leadership and the board - Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field required; CPA or MBA strongly preferred NICE TO HAVE - Experience in technology, SaaS, or creative AI sectors - Prior leadership within a venture-backed startup - Experience implementing or scaling financial systems or working with external partners WHAT WE OFFER - Competitive executive-level compensation - Substantial equity in a high-growth, mission-driven startup - Full health benefits, monthly stipends, and regular company retreats - Collaborative on-site office environment in Palo Alto (WFH Wednesdays) ABOUT PIKA At Pika, our mission is to make video creation radically seamless, deeply intuitive, and universally accessible. We're reimagining the creative process through AI and building a world-class team to push the limits of technology. Join us in Palo Alto, CA to help shape the future of creative technology and empower the next generation of creators.
